challenge: HQS Quantum Simulations NMR challenge, Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 (intermediate), repo kbarkhqs/qiskit-fall-fest, nmr.ipynb

initial_states.construction: H then RZ(phi_i) on every qubit, phi_i = pi * bit_i (0 -> |+>, pi -> |-> up to global phase -i); identical to RX(phi) then H
initial_states.number_of_states: 2^N (8 for A and B, 4 for C), all bit strings via itertools.product((0,1), repeat=N)
initial_states.eigenvalue_of_sum_X: N - 2w, w = number of qubits in |-> (not the bit label)
initial_states.weight_in_correlation_sum: m_n = N - 2w (measured as <sum X> at t=0); signed, not equal weights
caveats: weights are unique only up to scale: a*m+b (a != 0) gives a times the trace (Tr A(t) = 0 removes b), e.g. N-w = (m+N)/2 gives half, -(N-2w) minus the trace; normalised spectra identical (3e-16) because of the division by the maximum and np.abs
all-plus state alone: exact for C, off by 4.8 % (A) and 4.0 % (B) of the spectrum maximum
equal weights give 8.9e-16 rounding noise; guard now rejects signal scale < 1e-8

criterion.characteristic_peaks: maxima of the matched reference with height >= 0.05 and prominence >= 0.02 (normalised); components closer than 2 grid bins (2.667 Hz) merged
criterion.detection: each characteristic peak needs its own simulated local maximum within +-2.667 Hz, in order
criterion.separation_primary: dip between every pair of neighbouring characteristic peaks >= 10 % of the smaller maximum
criterion.search: noise_strength 0.1-100 in steps of 0.1, every pass/fail change refined in steps of 0.01

task_B_noise_tolerance.monotonic: exactly one pass->fail change per molecule and dip level; all pass at noise_strength = 0
robust_conclusions: molecule A has the lowest tolerance at every dip level >= 5 %
B vs C order is NOT robust: flips with dip level and with Trotter error (exact evolution: C 23.09 < B 23.48)
task_B_noise_tolerance.why_A_official_value_is_lower: first-order Trotter error changes line intensities by up to 19 % (A); swap test: exact positions + Trotter intensities = 28.00, Trotter positions + exact intensities = 32.45

molecule A.critical_splitting_origin: J12 - J02: inner lines of spin 2's doublet of doublets (5.48 ppm)

molecule B.critical_splitting_origin: J01 - J12: inner lines of spin 1's doublet of doublets (5.90 ppm)

molecule C.critical_splitting_origin: J01: outer, weaker lines of the AB quartet (roof effect)

j_coupling_answer.short: The tolerance is set by the smallest line spacing that must stay resolved, not by the J strength itself.
j_coupling_answer.observation: A has the largest couplings (mean |J| 10.2 Hz) and the lowest tolerance
j_coupling_answer.topology: A and B are near-chains (one coupling ~0); the central spin's doublet of doublets has an inner spacing equal to the DIFFERENCE of its two couplings (6.1 Hz in A, 7.0 Hz in B); C is an AB system with shift difference 4.6 J, outer lines 1.54x weaker
reviewer_tests: raising J02 and J12 together at fixed difference: threshold changes only -6 % / +2 %
changing only C's shift difference at fixed J: threshold changes by a factor 1.7
j_coupling_answer.rule_of_thumb: FWHM = Gamma/pi Hz; equal isolated lines D Hz apart lose their dip at Gamma = pi*sqrt(3)*D = 5.44 D (upper bound); measured ~3.3 D at 10 % dip, 4.4-4.8 D any dip

limitations: noise_strength is an artificial exponential window on an ideal simulation, not hardware noise
thresholds depend on the dip level: -16 % to +46 % between the 19 % and any-dip levels
A's 0.9 Hz J01 doublets are excluded (never two maxima on the 1.333 Hz grid); if required, A never passes
2-bin position tolerance is necessary (1 bin: A and B never pass even at noise 0)
splittings below about 3.5-4 Hz are never resolved with 300 steps of 2.5 ms
n = 3 molecules: across-molecule relation is correlation only; causal claim rests on one-coupling-at-a-time experiments
